title: Homemade instruments, Leo Watson and old neighbors
summary: Allen asks about washboard and jug players; talk drifts to Leo Watson, where Little Dad lived on St. Peter, and Joe Robichaux.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Ask him about all those funny instruments that you used to have, homemade instruments.

He said, how about all them homemade instruments you used to have, funny ones? Who made? Homemade. Homemade. Homemade instruments. Like washboards. Like washboards. Oh no, I don't know if you were there. Ask him who did.
Who did in them times?
I didn't know if this was funny, you know. Yeah. Yeah, we'll just- Sit on it.

Let me see. Let me see. Take it. What about the jug players? I was asking. He said, what about the jug players? He said, what about the jug players? Uh huh. The jug players? The jug? The jug. The jug. The jug. The jug. The jug.
The jug. The jug players. Oh, I used to hear that, but I didn't know that.
They're some of them with a hose pipe, too. Washboards.

The jug. The jug players. Oh, I used to hear that, but I didn't know them, you know. They're some of them with a hose pipe, too. Washboards. Soapbox for bass. But he doesn't know them. But you don't know them, you didn't know them, eh? No, I didn't know them. They used to have a fence for the reason to play for the open with these. Stools, you know, and there's some time. Every Friday and Saturday, we used to play two or three hours for them in the street. You know, like, get out in the river and all them big places. We used to have a bunch of them come around and dance, you know, they were kids. They were kids. They were good. They got a little bit older than they were in California. They ain't been back since. That was Dougie then. Yeah. Two brothers I know of them. They didn't even kick and bust it. They really could sing. They didn't even know them. Douglas Daniels. Is that the one you taught? Yeah. Yeah. Was with the spiritual rhythm. Yes. In New York.
That's right. That's right. That's right.
That's right. That's right.
That's right. That's right. That's right. That's right. That's right. That Leo Watson.
That kid.
Boy, that kid was good. That Leo Watson just killed me. Just kill me the same. I remember that.
Yeah. I know them all. I used to work at the Golden Looney Chicago. They used to, was in the show there, you know. When the show come on, they had a, you know, part in the show.
Was Leo Watson from around here or do you know where he was?
I don't know, but to tell me Del was, that's where I heard.
We're going to have to find out about Del.
Do you know that Joe Rubber show? Yeah. He used to play with us too.
He lives near Tom Albert. Tell him.
What?
Tell him he lives near Tom Albert.
Say he lives near Tom Albert. Tom Albert? He lives near Tom Albert. Oh, that's where you live in. Oh, yeah. What are you talking about, the piano? Yeah.
We all live down there. Tell him we all live.

They all live down there. Mmm. I got a friend that I lived down there. I didn't know she lived there yet. I used to live at Tom Albert too, you know. St. Peter between Bourbon and, what's the state I think? Royal? Huh? Dauphine or Royal? Yeah, Bourbon and Royal. Burbundi and, uh. Burbundi and, uh.

And Dolphine. And Bourbon, isn't it? Burbundi and Dauphine or Burgundi and Rambo? Yeah, Dauphine. Burbundi and Dauphine, yeah. Yeah, Dauphine. Yeah, Dauphine. Burbundi and Dauphine, yeah. Dauphine, I see it then.

She's very fair. Her name was Sadie Washington. She's living on this side of the person. Did she play music? No, she don't play music. Uptown, son. Oh, she's old, she's about four or five years old than me, you know. You used to have a real bright boy, you remember? Used to play a clarinet with us named Robeshow? Yeah, he's dead. What come of him? He's dead.
What was his name?

Get it, son. What was his first name? Huh? What was his first name? Joe Tick, I think Joe Robeshow. Joe Robeshow, yeah. Joe Robeshow, yeah. Yeah. He's a big clenny with Jack Hale-Band. Yeah. I never did know what come of him.
